page.layout: One page of running text, one column. Head: running title and page number at the top. Below the first line, a division heading "EXERCIT. III." with a subtitle, then the body text. Six printed quotation marks stand in the left margin beside the paragraph, with no text.

main_text.p: humano corpore, nihil esse aliud quàm e[?]-ius interitum. At hominis formam, quæ diuina essentia est, interire, nemo, nisi impius proferet. Verùm materiales formas, cuiusmodi sunt illæ brutorum, plantarum, & omnium imperfectorum corporum, euane-scere, ac in nihilum redigi, dum hæc corrumpuntur, ire inficias minimè uolumus.
main_text.head: EXERCIT. III.
CUR NON CORRUMPI POS-sit corporum materia?
main_text.p: RErum generabilium & corruptibilium materiam non interire, Fernelius ibidem ingenuè fatetur, sed causas non appositè uidetur reddere. Si enim (inquit) quando res oblitescit, illius materia simul interiret & disiparetur, communis rerum omnium moles iamdudum, uel fæ-pius esset absorpta, nec hominum uniuersum genus, nec rerum natura omnis, nec ipse mundus stare posset. Hæc Fernelij ratio adeò est infirma, ut nec uerisimilis, nec apparens uideatur. Nam si res, quæ intereunt in nihilum redigi contingeret, ealdem quoque ex nihilo fieri necessariò consequere-tur.

page.notes: The first word of the body paragraph is a large initial "R" joined to "Rerum". The first line "quàm e-ius" has an unclear letter after "quàm" (read as e, marked [?]). The word "ealdem" and "(inquit)" are as printed. Six small quotation marks stand in the left margin beside the body paragraph; they are printed marks, not text, and are not transcribed. No catchword, signature or footnote is printed. Long s is normalised to s throughout, for example "fcere" to "scere".
